hints.text: The CDN reduced origin traffic by serving cached content closer to users.
The GraphQL gateway is amplifying backend traffic through request fanout.
Retries are increasing total traffic and making failures spread faster.
Requests are waiting longer in queues because downstream systems are overloaded.
Autoscaling reacts with delay, so sudden bursts can still overload the platform.
Centralized authentication simplifies security but creates a shared dependency bottleneck.
The service mesh improved observability and retries, but added network overhead.
Low cache hit rates are forcing more requests to reach backend systems.
The ETL pipeline is delaying analytical data updates under heavy ingestion load.
The data warehouse isolated analytical workloads from production systems.
Edge filtering reduced malicious traffic before it reached core services.
Semantic retrieval improves relevance but adds retrieval latency and storage pressure.
AI inference workloads are saturating compute resources and increasing queue times.
Traffic was rerouted to healthier regions to maintain availability.
Deployments temporarily increase instability because systems are changing live.
The canary release limited the impact of unstable changes to a small user group.
Feature flags allowed risky functionality to be disabled without a rollback.
Observability systems generate massive write-heavy workloads at scale.
